items.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025
items.q: coach several bands that had the charge of playing the music of let’s say King Oliver or Jelly Roll Morton

ctx.x: I try not to think about chords initially. I try to think about sound and phrases. Melodic phrases. And then after I go for a while then I’m let’s see now, how many bars is this, what are the chords. And I might start to put chords on top of it or might not initially. I might wait to the end and try to figure out what they are. But I don’t want to be too constricted by structure and traditional structure. I want to kind of hear my own thing sometimes. Sometimes I use conventional structures very easily, like the…

pioneering in the fact that they’ve included early New Orleans jazz as part of their repertoire, and for several years before Covid I was a guest coach and I would go in and coach several bands that had the charge of playing the music of let’s say King Oliver or Jelly Roll Morton, and what they would do is they would have to transcribe the song. Everybody had to transcribe all the parts and then they would put it together and then they would all, you know, play the songs, and I would go in and talk about the…
Oh that’s such a great statement. Something that puts a hook in your ear.
